components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'

example.hanzi: 小孩子对什么都很好奇。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi duì shénme dōu hěn hàoqí.
example.english: Children are curious about everything.
example.fact: 好奇 pairs 好 in its less-common fourth-tone reading hào ("to be fond of," as in 好客) with 奇 ("strange, odd") — literally "fond of the strange," a fitting origin for a word meaning "curious." The far more frequent reading of 好, hǎo ("good"), is a different word entirely, so 好奇 is a small tone trap for learners who've only met 好 as hǎo.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 法庭对他进行了审判。
example.pinyin: Fǎtíng duì tā jìnxíngle shěnpàn.
example.english: The court put him on trial.
example.fact: 审 ("to examine closely," as in 审查) and 判 ("to judge, decide," as in 判断) combine transparently into "examine and judge" — a two-step compositional image that maps almost exactly onto what a trial actually is.

components.note: Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.

example.hanzi: 她一个人完成了这个项目,真了不起。
example.pinyin: Tā yí gè rén wánchéngle zhège xiàngmù, zhēn liǎobuqǐ.
example.english: She finished this project all by herself — that's really amazing.
example.fact: 了不起 uses the same "verb + 不起" potential-complement pattern behind 对不起 ("sorry," literally "cannot face [you]") and 买不起 ("can't afford," literally "cannot rise to buying") — here 了 ("to finish, come to an end") is the thing that "cannot be gotten past," giving 了不起 its sense of being unsurpassed, extraordinary.

meanings: base (of operations, industrial, military, research etc)

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这里曾经是一个军事基地。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ céngjīng shì yí gè jūnshì jīdì.
example.english: This used to be a military base.
example.fact: 基 alone means "foundation" (as in 基础, "basis") and 地 means "ground, place" — 基地 combines the two into a fairly literal "foundation-ground," the fixed operational site a military, industrial, or research effort is built on.

components.note: 亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')
讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.

example.hanzi: 让我们假设这个理论是对的。
example.pinyin: Ràng wǒmen jiǎshè zhège lǐlùn shì duì de.
example.english: Let's suppose this theory is correct.
example.fact: 假 here keeps its core sense "false, not real" (as in 假的, "fake") rather than its unrelated second reading jià ("vacation," as in 放假) — 假设 literally "to set up something not [yet] real," a vivid image for proposing a hypothesis.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — chatting involves listening as well as speaking.
卯 (mǎo) gives a sound distantly related to liáo, having drifted apart over time.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 我们常常在网上聊天。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chángcháng zài wǎngshàng liáotiān.
example.english: We often chat online.
example.fact: 天 in 聊天 doesn't mean "sky" or "day" here — it's a fossilized object noun bound to the verb 聊 ("to chat") that can't be swapped for a near-synonym, much like 架 is permanently fixed as the object of 打 in 打架 (also in this batch).

components.note: A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 除了他之外,大家都同意了。
example.pinyin: Chúle tā zhī wài, dàjiā dōu tóngyì le.
example.english: Except for him, everyone agreed.
example.fact: 之外 almost always closes out a "除了...之外" frame ("except for..."), and its 之 is the same literary possessive/linking particle behind 之前 ("before") and 之后 ("after") — a small family of formal, book-language location and time words built the same way.

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling woman.
疾 depicts someone struck by an arrow, an illness — paired with 女, it evokes a mind afflicted by envy, giving 嫉 its meaning 'jealous.'
女 (woman) — an older semantic link now largely faded from 妒's modern general meaning.
户 (hù) gives a sound distantly related to dù, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他非常嫉妒同事的成功。
example.pinyin: Tā fēicháng jídù tóngshì de chénggōng.
example.english: He's extremely jealous of his colleague's success.
example.fact: 嫉 and 妒 each independently mean "jealous, envious" on their own — 嫉妒 doubles up two near-synonymous characters into one word, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 elsewhere in this deck.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 借 describes an action between people, lending or borrowing.
昔 (xī) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jiè has diverged considerably.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 他总是找借口不来上班。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zhǎo jièkǒu bù lái shàngbān.
example.english: He's always finding excuses not to come to work.
example.fact: 借 means "to borrow" and 口 means "mouth, something said" — 借口 is literally a "borrowed word," a vivid image of reaching for someone else's ready-made line instead of stating your real reason.

components.note: 土 depicts a mound of earth resting on the ground — a simple picture of soil, giving 土 its meaning 'earth, soil, land.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这片土地非常肥沃。
example.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì fēicháng féiwò.
example.english: This land is very fertile.
example.fact: 土 and 地 both independently mean "earth, ground" — 土地 doubles up two near-synonymous "earth" characters into one word, the same pattern the pilot batch noted for 喜欢 and 应该.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
女 (woman) — 姆 names a woman who cares for children.
母 (mǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 姆's reading mǔ.

example.hanzi: 我们请了一位保姆照顾孩子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen qǐngle yí wèi bǎomǔ zhàogù háizi.
example.english: We hired a nanny to take care of the children.
example.fact: 姆 is a fairly rare character in modern Mandarin, surviving mainly in 保姆 and a small number of classical or dialectal words for a female caretaker — a case where an entire character's everyday use has narrowed down to almost a single word.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摇 describes shaking or waving something by hand.
䍃 (yáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 摇.
氵 (water) shows this relates to liquid, as in something boiling or rolling in water.
衮 (gǔn) gives the exact sound of 滚.

example.hanzi: 他很喜欢听摇滚音乐。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan tīng yáogǔn yīnyuè.
example.english: He really likes listening to rock music.
example.fact: 摇滚 is a phono-semantic loan translation of English "rock (and) roll" — 摇 ("to shake, sway") and 滚 ("to roll") were picked because their literal meanings echo the physical feel of the English term, not because Chinese needed brand-new native characters for the genre.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 妈妈慢慢放手,让孩子自己走。
example.pinyin: Māma mànmàn fàngshǒu, ràng háizi zìjǐ zǒu.
example.english: The mother slowly let go, letting the child walk on her own.
example.fact: 放手 is literally "to release the hand" (放 "to release" + 手 "hand"), and like English "let go" it spans both the physical action and the figurative sense of giving someone free rein or giving up a struggle.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows the action is done with the arms.
包 (to wrap) — wrapping your arms around something gives 抱 its meaning 'to hold, to hug.'
心 (heart) shows 怨 relates to an emotion.
夗 (yuàn) gives the exact sound of 怨.

example.hanzi: 他总是抱怨工作太累。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì bàoyuàn gōngzuò tài lèi.
example.english: He always complains that work is too tiring.
example.fact: 抱 keeps its core sense "to hold, embrace" (as in 抱着孩子, "holding a child"), so 抱怨 literally pictures someone "holding onto" 怨 (a grievance) rather than letting it go — a vivid image behind the everyday word for complaining.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 上课的时候要集中注意力。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhou yào jízhōng zhùyìlì.
example.english: You need to focus your attention during class.
example.fact: 注意力 builds on the two-character verb 注意 ("to pay attention," literally "to pour [one's] mind into something") by adding 力 ("strength, power") to turn the action into the noun naming the mental faculty itself — the same "verb + 力" pattern behind 理解力 ("comprehension") and 想象力 ("imagination").

components.note: 承 depicts multiple hands supporting and lifting something from below — giving 承 its meaning 'to support, to receive, to inherit.'
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 这座桥能承受很大的重量。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo néng chéngshòu hěn dà de zhòngliàng.
example.english: This bridge can bear a great deal of weight.
example.fact: 承 and 受 both independently carry a sense of "to receive" — 承 pictures hands lifting something from below, 受 pictures one hand passing something to another — together they form a word for withstanding pressure, whether physical, financial, or emotional.

meanings: to sign (one's name with a pen etc)

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early signature tallies and slips were made of bamboo.
佥 (qiān) is an exact match for the sound of 签.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 请在这里签名。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiānmíng.
example.english: Please sign here.
example.fact: 签's bamboo radical ⺮ reflects its original meaning, a bamboo slip or tally used as a marker or a lot-drawing stick in ancient China — 签名 extends that old idea of a marked, identifying token into the modern act of writing one's name to authenticate something.

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 这个牌子的衣服很时尚。
example.pinyin: Zhège páizi de yīfu hěn shíshàng.
example.english: This brand's clothes are very fashionable.
example.fact: 时 contributes "the times, the present era" (the same root behind 时间 and 时候), and 尚 carries a sense of "to esteem, hold in high regard" — 时尚 literally reads close to "what the times esteem," a fitting compositional image for "fashion, trend."

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 如果明天不下雨的话,我们就去爬山。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān bú xiàyǔ dehuà, wǒmen jiù qù páshān.
example.english: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
example.fact: 的话 tacks onto the end of a conditional clause to mark it as hypothetical, and it very often pairs redundantly with a leading 如果 ("if") — "如果...的话" double-marks the same "if" meaning at both ends of the clause, much like "因为...所以" keeps both halves in earlier batches of this deck.

components.note: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'
音 (sound/music) — represents a musical piece.
十 (ten) — ten musical movements or sections making up a complete piece gave 章 its meaning 'chapter, section, composition.'

example.hanzi: 他写了一篇很好的文章。
example.pinyin: Tā xiěle yì piān hěn hǎo de wénzhāng.
example.english: He wrote a very good article.
example.fact: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing patterns or tattoos, an old image of decoration that broadened into "writing, culture" — 文章 combines "writing" with 章 ("chapter, composition") into a word that names a complete, structured piece of writing.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
木 (wood) — racks and frames like 架 were traditionally built of wood.
加 (jiā) gives a rhyme close to jià, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 那两个孩子又打架了。
example.pinyin: Nà liǎng gè háizi yòu dǎjià le.
example.english: Those two kids got into a fight again.
example.fact: 架 in 打架 doesn't mean its usual "frame, rack" (as in 书架, "bookshelf") — it's a fossilized object noun bound only to 打, the same way 天 is fixed as the object of 聊 in 聊天 (also in this batch); neither noun can be swapped for a synonym.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 这种病毒传播得很快。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú chuánbò de hěn kuài.
example.english: This virus spreads very quickly.
example.fact: 病毒 was coined as a direct calque of the Western biomedical concept "virus," pairing 病 ("illness, disease") with 毒 ("poison, toxin") — and the same word does double duty for both a biological virus and a computer virus, just as "virus" does in English.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
Shell/money — represents wealth or tax paid.
Related to military affairs, since taxes historically funded armies.

example.hanzi: 她在音乐方面很有天赋。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè fāngmiàn hěn yǒu tiānfù.
example.english: She has a lot of talent in music.
example.fact: 赋 originally named a tax or levy exacted by the state (its 贝 "money" component ties to wealth, and its form has old links to military funding) — that sense of something imposed by authority later extended to the opposite direction, "to bestow, grant" (as in 赋予, "to endow with"), and 天赋 uses exactly that extended sense, framing a talent as something granted by heaven rather than earned.

components.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 他整天都在看书。
example.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān dōu zài kànshū.
example.english: He reads all day long.
example.fact: 整 carries a core sense of "whole, complete, orderly" that recurs in 整齐 ("neat") and 整理 ("to tidy up") — 整天 simply attaches that "whole" sense to 天 ("day") for "the entire day," the same pattern behind 整年 ("all year") and 整夜 ("all night").

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
氵 (water) — a beach or sandbar is found at the water's edge.
难 (difficult) contributes to the character's form, describing waters that are tricky to navigate near a shoal.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去海滩玩了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù hǎitān wán le.
example.english: We went to the beach over the weekend.
example.fact: 滩's 氵 (water) component signals its meaning of a sandbar or shoal at the water's edge, while its phonetic half 难 has drifted far from 滩's modern sound tān — 海滩 simply narrows that general "shoal" sense down to the specific case found by the sea.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

example.hanzi: 这家工厂的设备很先进。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng de shèbèi hěn xiānjìn.
example.english: This factory's equipment is very advanced.
example.fact: 设 means "to establish, set up" and 备 means "to prepare, get ready" — 设备 combines the two into a word for whatever has been set up and made ready for use, covering everything from factory machinery to household appliances.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 这个消息对他是个很大的打击。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi duì tā shì gè hěn dà de dǎjī.
example.english: This news was a huge blow to him.
example.fact: 打击 covers both a literal physical strike and a figurative psychological blow, the same double duty English "hit" performs in "hit hard" — as a verb it also means "to crack down on" (illegal activity, crime), extending "striking" into an enforcement sense with no single-word English equivalent.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 描 describes tracing or drawing something by hand.
苗 (miáo) is an exact match for the sound of 描.
辶 (to walk) — narrating something is like walking a listener through events
术 (shù) gives the sound — an exact match with 述's reading shù

example.hanzi: 请你描述一下事情发生的过程。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ miáoshù yíxià shìqing fāshēng de guòchéng.
example.english: Please describe how the incident happened.
example.fact: 描 keeps its core sense "to trace, sketch" (as in 描绘, "to depict") while 述 means "to narrate, recount" — 描述 pairs a visual, sketch-like image with a verbal, storytelling one, a fitting blend for the act of describing something in words.

meanings: likeness of a god or Buddha

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 庙里供着一座神像。
example.pinyin: Miào lǐ gòng zhe yí zuò shénxiàng.
example.english: There's a statue of a god enshrined in the temple.
example.fact: 像 shares its phonetic half 象 with the word for "elephant" purely for the sound xiàng, with no meaning connection between them — 神像 simply combines 神 ("god, deity") with 像's core sense "likeness, image" for a carved or painted representation of a deity.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī
疒 depicts a person lying sick in bed, the 'illness' radical.
了 here depicts a resolving action — clearing away an illness gave 疗 its meaning 'to treat, to cure.'

example.hanzi: 这家医院提供免费的医疗服务。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yīyuàn tígōng miǎnfèi de yīliáo fúwù.
example.english: This hospital provides free medical services.
example.fact: 医's oldest form is built around 矢 ("arrow"), reflecting its origin in treating battlefield arrow wounds — 医疗 pairs that ancient "healing" root with 疗 ("to cure, treat," itself built on the "sickbed" radical 疒) into the modern word for medical care in general.

components.note: 亻 (a person), shown twice — one person next to another, similar in shape, the source of 似's meaning 'to resemble, similar, like.'

example.hanzi: 他们俩的想法类似。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ de xiǎngfǎ lèisì.
example.english: The two of them have similar ideas.
example.fact: 似 pictures 亻 (a person) doubled, one figure next to another that resembles it — 类似 combines that image with 类 ("category, type") for things similar enough to belong to the same category, a slightly more formal register than the plainer 一样 seen earlier in this deck.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) suggests a hidden spot behind a hill.
急 (worried, urgent) suggests someone anxiously ducking out of sight, giving 隐 its meaning 'to hide, conceal.'
艹 (grass) — 藏 relates to hiding something among vegetation.
臧 (zāng) gives a rhyme close to cáng, sharing a similar initial.

example.hanzi: 他试图隐藏自己的真实想法。
example.pinyin: Tā shìtú yǐncáng zìjǐ de zhēnshí xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: He tried to hide his true thoughts.
example.fact: 藏's 艹 (grass) component reflects its original image of concealing something among vegetation, while 隐 pictures someone anxiously ducking out of sight behind a mound (阝) — 隐藏 doubles up two independently plausible "hiding" images into one word.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 她能说三种语言。
example.pinyin: Tā néng shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.
example.english: She can speak three languages.
example.fact: 言 is a pictograph of a mouth (口) with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out, an image of speaking, while 语 adds the phonetic 吾 to the same 讠 "speech" radical — 语言 doubles up two independently speech-related characters into the general word for "language."

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.

example.hanzi: 这不符合安全标准。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù fúhé ānquán biāozhǔn.
example.english: This doesn't meet the safety standard.
example.fact: 准's 冫 ("ice/water") component traces back to a carpenter's level that used a pool of water to check flatness — 标准 pairs that "true and level" sense with 标 ("mark, sign") for a fixed, agreed-upon mark other things are measured against.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他对音乐充满激情。
example.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè chōngmǎn jīqíng.
example.english: He is full of passion for music.
example.fact: 激 originally described water dashing forcefully against something (氵 "water" plus the phonetic 敫) — 激情 extends that image of a forceful surge of water to emotion, giving "passion" a literal sense of feeling that rushes and crashes rather than sits still.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù
身 — depicts a drawn bow
寸 — a hand releasing the arrow

example.hanzi: 医生给他做了一次注射。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā zuòle yí cì zhùshè.
example.english: The doctor gave him an injection.
example.fact: 注 keeps its core sense "to pour" (as in 注意, literally "to pour one's mind [into something]"), and 射 pictures a drawn bow (身) with a hand releasing the arrow (寸) — 注射 combines "to pour" with "to shoot," a fittingly forceful image for pushing liquid into the body with a needle.

components.note: A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他刚买了一辆新车子。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng mǎile yí liàng xīn chēzi.
example.english: He just bought a new car.
example.fact: 车 is a simplified form of 車, itself a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above, wheels and axle visible in the shape — 子 here is the same light, semantically bleached suffix seen in 孩子 (also in this deck), turning the bare noun "cart, vehicle" into the everyday colloquial word for one.

components.note: 门 (gate, door) shows 阁 relates to a type of building with an entrance.
各 (gè) gives a sound close to gé, differing mainly in tone.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 阁下,请往这边走。
example.pinyin: Géxià, qǐng wǎng zhè biān zǒu.
example.english: Your excellency, please come this way.
example.fact: 阁 originally named a raised pavilion or high building (as in 阁楼, "attic"), and 下 here works like the "below" in English "Your Highness" — 阁下 literally addresses someone as speaking from "below your tower," an indirect, deferential way of naming a person of high rank without naming them directly.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 他把这只猫当作自己的孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhè zhī māo dàngzuò zìjǐ de háizi.
example.english: He treats this cat as if it were his own child.
example.fact: 当 here takes its less common fourth-tone reading dàng ("to regard as, to treat as"), not the far more frequent first-tone dāng ("to act as, when," as in 当时) — mixing up the two tones is an easy, common slip for learners meeting 当作 for the first time.

meanings: to be in (some state, position, or condition)

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 这个国家目前处于经济危机之中。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā mùqián chǔyú jīngjì wēijī zhī zhōng.
example.english: This country is currently in an economic crisis.
example.fact: 处 here takes its third-tone reading chǔ ("to deal with, to be situated," as in 处理), not the fourth-tone chù used for its noun sense "place, location" (as in 到处, "everywhere") — the same character splits cleanly between a "place" reading and a "to be positioned/deal with" reading depending on tone.

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — historically linked to a wary, hesitant animal, extended to mean 'as if, similar to.'
尤 (yóu) is an exact match for the sound of 犹.
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他的很多朋友都是犹太人。
example.pinyin: Tā de hěn duō péngyou dōu shì Yóutàirén.
example.english: Many of his friends are Jewish.
example.fact: 犹太 is a phonetic transliteration of "Judea/Judah," with 犹 and 太 chosen purely for their sound and carrying no meaning of their own here — 人 ("person") is simply appended the same way it is in 中国人 or 美国人 to turn a place or people name into "a person of that people."

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'

example.hanzi: 请写一份论文提要。
example.pinyin: Qǐng xiě yí fèn lùnwén tíyào.
example.english: Please write an abstract for the paper.
example.fact: 提 keeps its core sense "to lift, raise, bring up" (as in 提问, "to raise a question"), and 要 here means "the essentials, the important points" — 提要 literally "to draw out the essentials," a fittingly literal name for a document that extracts a text's key points.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 投 relates to throwing something with the hand
殳 (shū) gives a loose sound connection to 投's reading tóu
贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 他把钱投资在了房地产上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián tóuzī zàile fángdìchǎn shàng.
example.english: He invested his money in real estate.
example.fact: 投 keeps its core sense "to throw, to cast" (as in 投球, "to throw a ball"), so 投资 literally pictures "throwing" one's 资 (funds, capital) into something — a vivid, if slightly risky-sounding, image for the act of investing.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 你这样说有点过分了。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shuō yǒudiǎn guòfèn le.
example.english: What you just said is a bit excessive.
example.fact: 过 carries a core sense of "to pass, to cross over" (as in 过去, "to pass by, the past"), so 过分 literally means "to cross over the [proper] division" (分) — going past the line that marks what's reasonable or appropriate.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.

example.hanzi: 他还没有女朋友,一直在找对象。
example.pinyin: Tā hái méiyǒu nǚpéngyou, yìzhí zài zhǎo duìxiàng.
example.english: He doesn't have a girlfriend yet — he's still looking for a partner.
example.fact: 对象 covers both a neutral, abstract sense ("target, object [of study or action]") and a distinctly colloquial one, "boyfriend or girlfriend" — 找对象 ("to look for a partner") is the standard, extremely common way to talk about dating and marriage prospects in everyday Mandarin.

meanings: to see each other for a bit

components.note: 冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 我们找个时间见见吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo gè shíjiān jiàn jian ba.
example.english: Let's find some time to meet up.
example.fact: 见见 reduplicates the single verb 见 ("to see, to meet") to soften and shorten the action into "meet for a bit" — the same casual reduplication pattern behind 看看 ("take a look") and 想想 ("think it over"), which is why the second syllable's tone typically flattens to neutral in speech (jiàn jian, not jiàn jiàn).

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect
至 (zhì) gives the sound — 致 is also pronounced zhì, an exact match

example.hanzi: 大家的意见很一致。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā de yìjiàn hěn yízhì.
example.english: Everyone's opinions are very much in agreement.
example.fact: 一致 attaches 一 ("one") to 致 ("to arrive at, bring about") for a literal "arriving at one [point]" — the compositional image behind the modern sense "in agreement, unanimous," much like English "come to one mind" describes the same convergence.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 医生把病人转移到了另一间病房。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng bǎ bìngrén zhuǎnyí dàole lìng yì jiān bìngfáng.
example.english: The doctor transferred the patient to another ward.
example.fact: 转 keeps its core sense "to turn, to change direction" (车, "cart," reflecting the image of a turning wheel), and 移 independently means "to move, shift" — 转移 combines "turning" with "moving" for relocating something, whether a patient, funds, or someone's attention.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他负责管理这家公司。
example.pinyin: Tā fùzé guǎnlǐ zhè jiā gōngsī.
example.english: He's in charge of managing this company.
example.fact: 管 originally named a bamboo pipe or tube (⺮, "bamboo"), later extending metaphorically to "to control, to be in charge of" — much as English "channel" can drift from a literal waterway to an organizational sense, 管 drifted from a physical tube to administrative oversight.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
宓 depicts stillness and quiet beneath a roof.
山 (mountain) — a quiet, secluded mountain gave 密 its meaning 'dense, secret, close.'

example.hanzi: 这份文件的内容必须保密。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn de nèiróng bìxū bǎomì.
example.english: The contents of this document must be kept confidential.
example.fact: 保 keeps its core sense "to protect, look after" (its own etymology traces to a caretaker cradling a child), and 密 means "dense, secret, close" — 保密 literally "to protect the secret," treating confidentiality as something actively guarded rather than just withheld.
